title: Western Disturbances: Winter Rain in the North

endcard.line: Pictures: Vyacheslav Argenberg (CC BY 4.0); Rudolph A. Furtado (CC0). Footage: Thomas Bresson (CC BY 3.0)

segments.say: The monsoon is long gone. It's January. So why is it snowing in Kashmir and raining in Punjab?

anim.title: A long journey
items: Storms form over the Mediterranean region

segments.say: The answer comes from far away. Storms that form over the Mediterranean region are carried east, across West Asia, by strong westerly winds high in the sky.
In India we call them western disturbances. They arrive one after another, mostly from December to February.
When they meet the Himalayas, the moist air rises and cools. The hills get snow, and the plains below get light winter rain.

anim.title: Why farmers care
items: Rain for wheat and other rabi crops
Snow that feeds rivers in summer
Cold waves and fog after they pass

segments.say: That winter rain matters. It waters the rabi crops, especially wheat. The snow melts in summer and feeds the rivers.
So the north gets rain from two directions. The monsoon from the south-west seas in summer, and western disturbances from the west in winter.
For GS One: Mediterranean origin, carried by the westerlies, winter rain in the north-west, good for the rabi crop.

sources: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 4 (Climate): western cyclonic disturbances originate over the Mediterranean Sea, are brought into India by the westerly jet stream, cause winter rainfall in the north-western plains, which is beneficial for rabi crops; snowfall in the Himalayas
IMD Glossary, 'Western Disturbance': an extra-tropical storm from the Mediterranean region bringing winter rain to north-west India

quiz.why: They begin over the Mediterranean region and travel east.

options: Westerly winds high in the sky
quiz.why: The westerly jet stream carries them east.

quiz.q: Which crop benefits most from their rain?
quiz.why: Winter rain in the north-west waters the rabi crop.
